THE INFRASTRUCTURE

One server.
Clear paths.

A single-VPS gateway with separate paths for encrypted traffic, private DNS and administration.

Select a component to read its role below. DNS and the dashboard are private to the VPN; server administration uses SSH.

01 / THE VPN PATH

strongSwan → IPv4 Internet

Your phone establishes an IKEv2/IPsec tunnel using EAP-MSCHAPv2. The VPS terminates it and forwards IPv4 traffic. Other Android users can use the official strongSwan app. The administrator can use Rookstride’s embedded engine.

02 / THE DNS PATH

AdGuard Home → Unbound

VPN clients use private DNS on the same VPS. AdGuard applies the chosen blocklist; Unbound recursively resolves allowed names. DNS port 53 and the dashboard stay private. AAAA answers are suppressed because this gateway intentionally has no IPv6 Internet exit.

03 / THE MANAGEMENT PATH

Pinned SSH → local helper

The administrator’s app verifies and pins the SSH host key. It uploads the bundled installer and sends bounded requests to a root-only helper. VICI is a local Unix socket; the AdGuard API is private. No public Rookstride management service or cloud account is involved.

04 / THE OPTIONAL HISTORY

Local counters → SQLite

A small optional Python collector samples payload counters every 30 seconds and listens for disconnect/rekey events. Its SQLite history stays on your VPS. The app reads it over SSH. It estimates usage; it does not inspect traffic contents or identify physical hardware.

THE EDGES MATTER

Know what
crosses where.

Useful defaults, with explicit boundaries.

Tunnel profile
MTU 1280, full IPv4/IPv6 selectors and outside-tunnel blocking while the VPN is active.
IPv6
The gateway intentionally sinks IPv6 traffic and suppresses AAAA DNS answers. IPv4 Internet egress is supported.
Administration
Rookstride’s own SSH and certificate-fetch traffic is exempt from its tunnel, so gateway management remains reachable. Other apps use the VPN.
When disconnected
Use and test Android’s Always-on VPN / Block connections without VPN settings for disconnected lockdown. The app does not configure that OS setting silently.
Private services
DNS and the AdGuard dashboard stay private. Inbound public ports are your SSH port and IKEv2 UDP 500/4500.

ACCESS YOU CAN EXPLAIN

People, profiles
and permission.

Administrator access stays with the administrator. Invitations carry only what a VPN user needs.

Shared login

Several simultaneous sessions can use one account. Totals aggregate under that login. Revoking it affects every copy.

Separate device login

A separate EAP login makes individual revocation and estimates clearer. Labels are administrator supplied; copied credentials can still be used elsewhere.

Password-free export

A .sswan profile pins the server certificate and carries the login. Send the VPN password separately. It never contains root/SSH access.

A session is not a hardware identity.

Public endpoint addresses can change or be shared behind NAT. IPsec cannot reliably discover a phone model or a router’s hostname. Certificate-bound device authentication is a future gate, not an alpha2 feature.

Disconnect closes a selected session; a client may reconnect automatically. Revoke removes the login and attempts to close its sessions, preventing new authentication.

SMALL SERVICE / HONEST TOTALS

Observe the route.
Keep the cost visible.

The optional collector runs locally with a 64 MiB memory limit and 5% CPU quota. Those are protective service limits, not a whole-stack capacity guarantee.

30 sCounter sampling, plus rekey/disconnect events
UTCCalendar-month estimates, beginning at enrollment
LocalSQLite history, read through administrator SSH

A short, single-client 40-second sample on a one-CPU VPS with about 1.92 GiB RAM measured 15,516 KiB collector RSS and 0.025% of one CPU core. This is not a sustained-load benchmark. A 1-core/1-GB VPS remains a capacity test target.

Inactive session/counter detail expires after 30 days and is capped at 10,000 rows; daily totals retain 400 days. Monitoring gaps are exposed. Encryption overhead and traffic missed during an outage are not fully reflected, so these are operational estimates rather than billing records.
